The cancelled rebuild has exit 143 and never started, so this worktree has no store. discoveries: (1) The ticket was not claimed at the start of run 1: it is still `open` and its role is still the independent auditor. (2) `gov.retrieval.measure` has no form-only mode. `--part visible` runs a retrieval for each of the 24 visible files and needs a store, so my brief has the designer check the form with a script that calls the measure's own loader on q21 to q24 only. (3) About six rebuilds were waiting on `/tmp/gov-os-rebuild.lock`, the oldest for 51 minutes. (4) Tripwire: nothing changed in this worktree or the main tree. In `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-91-tests`, 11 untracked dotfiles and folders appeared (.bash_profile, .bashrc, .gitconfig, .gitmodules, .idea, .mcp.json, .profile, .ripgreprc, .vscode, .zprofile, .zshrc), and the tripwire also flagged its acceptance folder W2-91. That is another ticket's worker; my worker never started.
risks: The role file in this worktree does not yet give the test designer `fixtures/evaluation/**`. After the claim, the guard may still refuse the designer's writes unless the role file's paths or the ticket's role are updated together with the status.
lessons: Claim the ticket (status `in_progress`, role `independent-test-designer`, the role file carrying DEC-996 (B)'s write path) before starting its lead. For a test designer, retrieving from W2-00-store avoids the rebuild queue.
